scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “A Low-Space Algorithm for Worst-Case Subset Sum” (preprints/A-Low-Space-Algorithm-for-Worst-Case-Subset-Sum-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 138 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 88f951cb233cf765), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a single uniform classical randomized algorithm in this model that never answers YES incorrectly and answers each YES instance correctly with probability at least 2/3. For every fixed positive integer c, there are a constant Ac > 0 and positive integers kc, Nc such that, whenever n ≥ Nc and b ≤ nc, every outcome of the algorithm’s randomness uses at most Acnkc 2n/2 operations and Ac(n + b + 2)15 20.199n writable words. The algorithm does not depend on c.
